items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
Your grandparents may say one rupee once equalled one dollar. Today a dollar costs about ninety-five. Was it ever true?
Chars
[nervous, squeaky banknote, trembling] Ninety-five of you, for one of me?
Narrator
So when was a rupee worth a dollar?
Narrator
In nineteen forty-seven? Never. Sorry, Grandpa. A dollar cost about three point three rupees.
Narrator
It was tied to the British pound, not the dollar.
Narrator
In nineteen sixty-six, after a war and a drought, India devalued to seven point five.
Narrator
In nineteen ninety-one, India nearly ran out of dollars. A year later: past thirty.
Narrator
And here's the part almost nobody mentions.
Narrator
A falling rupee isn't always failure. It makes Indian exports cheaper.
Narrator
That's the mirage: the golden age of one rupee, one dollar never existed.
Narrator
Near a record low, the real question isn't the rupee. It's whether your income outruns the dollar.
Narrator
Comment: what did your grandparents tell you?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
